items.question: Which BNS section replaced IPC Section 302?
items.answer: IPC §302 (Punishment for murder) corresponds to BNS §103 (Punishment for murder). The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 with effect from 1 July 2024.

sources.title: Punishment for murder
sources.name: IPC 1860, Section 302
sources.text: IPC 1860, Section 302 - Punishment for murder (replaced by BNS 2023 Section 103) Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

sources.title: Punishment for murder
sources.name: BNS 2023, Section 103
sources.text: BNS 2023, Section 103 - Punishment for murder (corresponds to IPC 1860 Section 302) Chapter 6: Offences Affecting The Human Body 103. (1) Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. (2) When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

items.question: Is mischief still dealt with under IPC Section 425?
items.verdict: No — and four old sections were folded together
items.answer: No. The Indian Penal Code, 1860 was repealed with effect from 1 July 2024. IPC §425 (Mischief) now corresponds to BNS §324 (Mischief), which consolidates IPC §425, IPC §426, IPC §427, IPC §440 into a single provision.

items.question: Which BNS section corresponds to IPC Section 124A?
items.answer: None. IPC §124A (Sedition) has no counterpart in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The official BPRD correspondence table lists no BNS equivalent for it, so any section number offered in reply is wrong by construction.

items.chip: Is BNSS 482 the same as CrPC 482?
items.question: Does BNSS Section 482 deal with the same subject as CrPC Section 482?
items.answer: No. CrPC §482 (Saving of inherent power of High Court) corresponds to BNSS §528, not to BNSS §482. BNSS §482 is a different provision entirely — Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest — which corresponds to CrPC §438.

items.chip: Is theft bailable under the BNS?
items.question: Is an offence under BNS Section 303 bailable?
items.answer: Under the First Schedule to the BNSS, an offence under BNS §303 (Theft) is cognizable and non-bailable, triable by Any Magistrate. Punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for not be less than 1 year but which may extend to 5 years and fine.

items.question: Which IPC sections correspond to BNS Section 115?
items.answer: BNS §115 (Voluntarily causing hurt) corresponds to IPC §321 and IPC §323. No single IPC section accounts for it on its own.

items.chip: What single BNS section replaced IPC 171?
items.question: Which single BNS section replaced IPC Section 171?
items.answer: There is no single one. IPC §171 (Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent) was split across BNS §177, BNS §205. Citing only one of them states the position incompletely.

items.chip: An offence on 15 August 2024 — which code?
items.question: An offence was committed on 15 August 2024. Does the IPC or the BNS apply?
items.answer: The BNS applies. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 came into force on 1 July 2024, so an offence committed on 15 August 2024 is dealt with under the BNS. The IPC continues to govern offences committed before that date, and proceedings already begun under the old codes continue under them.
